spans.s: jāṅgala (IA 18), cf. s-ānūpa-jāṅgala, an epithet of the gift land; either ‘arid’ or ‘covered with jungle’.

jaṅgama, cf. sa-sthāvara jaṅgama (IE 8-5); the moveable belongings of a village.
 (SITI), a priest of the Liṅgāyat or Vīraśaiva sect.
jaṅghā (HRS), forced service as messenger, as indicated by the Jātakas; also same as Jaṅghākarika.
Jaṅghākarika (HRS), ‘one who pays the royal dues by means of his legs’; ‘one who is liable to compulsory service as a messenger’, according to the Amarakośa. Same as Jaṅghā (q. v.).
jaṅghāla, an embankment (JAS, Letters, Vol. XX, p. 204).
Jāṅghika (HRS), same as Jaṅghā or Jaṅghākarika.
